architecture_principles: the unit of decision is an experiment, not a formulation
value of information is computed by a deterministic scientific tool, not by an additional language model
every registered hypothesis carries an explicit pre-result prediction rule and an explicit falsification condition
a measurement that cannot separate any registered hypothesis scores zero discrimination, and that is a scientific result rather than a defect
weight sensitivity is reported as decision stability, never as model confidence
ties in the deterministic layer are reported as ties; the tool must not manufacture a preference it does not have
held-out result data are structurally removed before any payload is assembled
the mechanism question and the Agent framework are separate contributions and are reported separately

candidate_space.rationale: V4 deliberately reuses the byte-identical V3 lattice. Continuous-space optimization and any new wet-lab work are out of scope, so that the measured change between V3 and V4 is the decision object and the VOI layer, not the search space.

architecture.canonical_flow: planner(intent + failure mode) -> evidence/tool layer (including the deterministic VOI tool) -> proposer -> skeptic -> robustness adjudicator -> judge -> freeze
architecture.claim_boundary: V4.0.0 selects an experiment from pre-result evidence under an outcome-blind runtime. Its adjudication tests whether a registered hypothesis survives contact with the completed measurement. It is not a contemporaneous pre-experimental record and does not claim that the historical decision used this ranking.
architecture.name: PUR_NEW_VOI_GUIDED_EXPERIMENT_SELECTION_AGENT_V4
non_goals: adding a language model to compute value of information
adding Agent roles beyond planner, tools, proposer, skeptic, robustness adjudicator, judge and freeze
turning the study into a pure AI benchmark
weakening or replacing the rheological mechanism result
architecture.purpose: Outcome-blind scientific decision Agent that selects the next formulation x measurement EXPERIMENT by transparent value of information, rather than selecting a formulation candidate alone.

stages.role: identify the physical failure mode and the scientific question that the next experiment must answer, then request the evidence needed to judge experiments rather than formulations

execute read-only scientific tools, including the paper-derived state-aware rheology tool, external evidence retrieval, and the deterministic VOI tool that scores every formulation x measurement experiment card
propose the experiment with the highest scientific information value, stating the hypotheses it separates and what each possible outcome would establish
attack the proposed experiment on hypothesis coverage, confounding, interpretability of the primary observable, and whether the stated falsification criterion can actually be met by the measurement
adjudicate whether the proposed experiment survives the reported VOI weight sensitivity and the skeptic's strongest objection
commit to one experiment card, or abstain, and state the acceptance and falsification criteria that will adjudicate it
programmatically validate and freeze the experiment card with timestamps, model identifiers and cryptographic hashes of every input

architecture.supersedes_nothing: V4 is an independent architecture. configs/agent_v3.json, prompts/agent_v3_*.txt, src/pur_new/agent_v3.py and every frozen V3 run record remain unchanged and are not reinterpreted by V4.

voi_tool.explicitly_not: distance to any held-out formulation. No target coordinate enters any component, weight or tie-break.
voi_tool.formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk
voi_tool.name: score_experiment_cards
voi_tool.not_a_posterior: The local design contains six audited realizations and two thermal-hold trajectories. That does not support a calibrated Bayesian expected-information computation, so no posterior probability is fabricated. Weight sensitivity is reported instead.

evidence_policy.description: For prospective/blind Agent evaluation. The Agent may see original-system measurements and external analogue evidence, but not the target validation formulation identity, its wet-lab outcome, or any outcome-derived labels.

judge_normalized.acceptance_criterion: Accept transfer of the H-CORE baseline prediction if the mean SI_15_60 is between 7.51% and 11.51%, inclusive, corresponding to 9.51% plus or minus the registered 2.00 percentage-point resolution.
judge_normalized.falsification_criterion: If mean SI_15_60 is at or below 7.50%, the transferred H-CORE linear prediction of 9.51% is falsified on the registered low-drift side by more than 2.00 percentage points. If mean SI_15_60 is at or above 11.52%, the quantitative E1-to-E2 baseline transfer is rejected upward, but this does not formally falsify H-CORE under its registered low-side falsification rule. No numerical outcome from this unmodified candidate falsifies H-RESIN or H-DUAL.
judge_normalized.next_experiment_if_falsified: Run S1C02::M-REPEAT to determine whether controlled preparation reduces the documented E2 realization spread; after state control, run process-matched M-HOLD-120 cards for an E2-centered acrylic-only candidate and an E2-centered acrylic-plus-minor-tackifier candidate to adjudicate H-RESIN and H-DUAL.

judge_normalized.rationale: This is a defensible baseline probe rather than a mitigation formulation. planner.failure_mode: Uncontrolled viscosity growth during prolonged 120 C melt residence, with hold stability unresolved for the E2-anchored candidate space.
planner.failure_mode_evidence: In the original 120 C thermal-hold data, E5 viscosity increased by 51.54% from 15 to 60 min and by 93.08% from 15 to 90 min. E1 increased by 9.51% and 16.85% over the same windows, showing substantial formulation-dependent drift; no E2 hold trajectory is measured.
planner.least_resolved_justification: Temperature response is measured from 80 to 130 C for multiple formulations, and realized viscosity-level variability is quantified for E2 with three runs at each temperature. In contrast, the isothermal coordinate has only one 120 C trajectory each for E1 and E5, with no measured E2 trajectory and no independent hold repeats. Thus drift for the reactive-core anchor and modifier candidates is unmeasured.
measurement_requirements: Measure the candidate directly under the registered matched-window 120 C hold protocol at 15, 30, 45, and 60 min, without extrapolation beyond the measured window.
Use at least two independent preparations and report each raw trajectory, the 15-to-60 min relative viscosity change, and repeat-to-repeat uncertainty.
Record and control preparation and melt-history variables because E2 temperature-sweep realizations differ by approximately 2.80-fold to 3.57-fold at matched temperatures.
Determine the candidate reactive mass fraction and freeze the H-CORE linear-dilution prediction, E1 drift multiplied by reactive mass fraction, before observing the result.
Compare measured drift with the preregistered 2 percentage-point discrimination threshold and with the H-RESIN criterion of drift below half the linear-dilution prediction.

Require candidate experiment cards to identify whether the acrylic-like axis, minor-tackifier-like axis, or both are active so that an outcome can distinguish H-CORE from H-RESIN and, where composition permits, test the tackifier requirement in H-DUAL.
Retain the realized viscosity at 15 min as a separate level coordinate rather than interpreting reduced initial viscosity as improved hold stability.
planner.scientific_question: At a known reactive mass fraction, do acrylic-like and/or minor tackifier-like modifiers reduce 120 C viscosity drift only by linear dilution of the reactive core, suppress drift substantially beyond linear dilution, or require a nonzero minor-tackifier axis to reach the low-drift regime?

outcome_interpretation.if_acceptance_criterion_met: Drift below 4.75% across at least two repeats would falsify the registered E1-based H-CORE prediction of 9.51% for this E2 core, by more than the 2 percentage-point resolution threshold. Because no resin modifier is present, this would reveal an unexpectedly low E2-core baseline or reference-transfer failure; it would not establish H-RESIN or falsify H-DUAL.
outcome_interpretation.if_falsification_criterion_met: Drift at or above 9.51% would rule out an anomalously low E2-core baseline. Agreement with 9.51% within the 2 percentage-point resolution supports H-CORE at this unmodified anchor; a substantially higher value would instead show that the E1-based linear reference does not transfer quantitatively. This core-only outcome cannot validly falsify H-RESIN or H-DUAL because neither modifier axis is active.
outcome_interpretation.if_intermediate: Drift between 4.75% and 9.51% would indicate partial departure from the E1-based core prediction without reaching the preregistered strong-suppression regime. A deficit exceeding 2 percentage points would challenge H-CORE, but the absence of modifiers would leave H-RESIN and H-DUAL unresolved and would require a subsequent resin-modified hold experiment.

proposer.primary_observable: SI_15_60 = (eta_60 - eta_15) / eta_15, percent, measured directly during the 120 C hold

ranked_alternatives.why_lower_value: It is E1-like and would mainly replicate a core composition that already has a measured 120 C hold trajectory, whereas the E2 anchor has no hold data.
It is a measured reactive-core composition but is not the E2-centered anchor identified by the planner as the unresolved basis of the modifier candidate space.
It directly addresses realization-state control, but it measures viscosity-scale spread rather than the isothermal drift coordinate on which H-CORE, H-RESIN, and H-DUAL disagree.

proposer.reasoning: M-HOLD-120 directly measures the declared failure mode over the matched 15-60 minute window and avoids regression, extrapolation, or imputation. S1C02 fills the specific missing E2 hold baseline and should use at least two independent preparations with fully recorded process histories. However, it activates neither externally supported modifier axis and its registered predictions are identical for all three hypotheses, so it separates zero hypothesis pairs. Its value is therefore baseline resolution rather than adjudication of resin suppression or tackifier necessity.
proposer.tie_break_justification: S1C02 is the measured E2 reactive-core anchor, exactly matching the planner's unresolved candidate-space baseline. Unlike E1, E2 has no existing hold trajectory, while its large 2.80-3.57-fold realization spread makes replicated, process-recorded measurement especially important. Thus S1C02 provides greater marginal baseline information than the other deterministically tied core-only cards without relying on card order.

residual_decision_risk: The experiment separates zero registered hypothesis pairs and cannot test resin suppression or tackifier necessity.
The 9.51% benchmark is transferred from E1 despite differences in reactive-core composition and NCO:OH ratio, so disagreement does not uniquely falsify H-CORE.
M-HOLD-120 does not itself control process state, while E2 has shown a 3.57-fold viscosity spread at 120 C; preparation and melt history must be matched and enforced across independent repeats.
The card-level acceptance and falsification language for H-RESIN and H-DUAL remains scientifically invalid unless explicitly relabeled as baseline-transfer interpretation.

The tied top set consists entirely of core-only hold cards, so its tie does not identify an experiment that separates the modifier hypotheses; exact IDs for suitable modifier candidates were not supplied.
Weight-perturbation robustness cannot be adjudicated because the decision-stability sweep outputs were withheld.
The direct rheological observable cannot establish the molecular encounter-frequency explanation stated within H-RESIN.
robustness_adjudication.skeptic_objection_reasoning: The objection invalidates interpreting this core-only experiment as accepting or falsifying H-RESIN or H-DUAL: S1C02 activates neither modifier axis, all three hypotheses predict 9.51%, and zero hypothesis pairs are separated. It does not invalidate M-HOLD-120 as a direct measurement of the missing E2 thermal-hold baseline. The proposer already characterizes its purpose as baseline resolution and states that H-RESIN and H-DUAL remain unresolved. Results must therefore be restricted to E2 baseline transfer, with deviations from 9.51% potentially reflecting E1-to-E2 core differences or realization-state variation. A modifier design would be required in a subsequent experiment to adjudicate the registered modifier hypotheses.
robustness_adjudication.weight_sensitivity_assessment: S1C02::M-HOLD-120 is one of nine tied top-score hold experiments, each with VOI score 0.2435, although the rule-order presentation places S1C01::M-HOLD-120 first. The decision-stability report was withheld and supplies no top_experiment_set_stability, base_margin_to_first_strictly_lower, or recommendation_flip_boundary values. Therefore, the perturbations that would change the tied top set and their scientific defensibility cannot be determined from the supplied payload.

skeptic.falsification_criterion_assessment: The apparatus can produce SI_15_60 values below 4.75%, within 2 percentage points of 9.51%, or at/above 9.51%. Thus a numerical challenge to the transferred E1-based E2-core prediction is attainable. The stated full falsification criterion is not scientifically attainable, however, because H-RESIN requires a resin-modified composition and H-DUAL requires an acrylic-only composition to test tackifier necessity; S1C02 has 0.0% acrylic and 0.0% tackifier. The proposer’s narrative outcome interpretation correctly narrows the result to baseline transfer, but the card-level acceptance and falsification language does not.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A low E2-core drift could be misrepresented as evidence for H-RESIN even though no resin modifier was tested, and no result could adjudicate H-DUAL.
objections.objection: S1C02 has AC1920 = 0.0%, TK100 = 0.0%, and reactive_mass_fraction = 1.0000, so all three registered predictions are 9.51% and hypothesis_discrimination_detail reports zero separated pairs. It therefore cannot test resin suppression or tackifier necessity. The proposer correctly declares H-CORE vs H-RESIN, H-CORE vs H-DUAL, and H-RESIN vs H-DUAL as unseparated, but the card-level acceptance criterion incorrectly says drift below 4.75% would accept H-RESIN over H-CORE.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: Deviation from 9.51% could be attributed incorrectly to failure of H-CORE rather than E1-to-E2 core non-transferability or preparation-state variation.
objections.objection: The 9.51% prediction for S1C02 is transferred from E1 even though E1 has NCO:OH = 1.7 and MDI/PDP70/PPG2000 fractions of 19.2867/40.3567/40.3567%, while S1C02/E2 has NCO:OH = 1.8 and fractions of 20.1907/39.9047/39.9047%. Thus a difference from 9.51% is confounded with reactive-core composition and stoichiometry rather than isolating dilution or modifier effects. In addition, M-HOLD-120 is marked controls_process_state = false despite E2 showing a 3.57-fold viscosity spread at 120 C; recording process history without specifying and enforcing matched controls does not remove this state confound.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The measurement may be correctly read while the hypothesis comparison based on its benchmark remains unsupported.
objections.objection: No material interpretability defect exists for the primary observable itself: SI_15_60 is calculated directly from measured eta_15 and eta_60 at 120 C, with no model fit, extrapolation, or imputation. However, interpreting that direct value against the transferred E1-derived 9.51% benchmark still inherits the cross-core assumption identified under confounding.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: Observable numerical outcomes would be treated as falsifications of hypotheses whose required modifier conditions were never instantiated.
objections.objection: The card-level falsification criterion is not valid for the full registered hypothesis set. It says H-RESIN is falsified at drift greater than or equal to 9.51%, but the registry restricts that condition to a resin-modified composition and S1C02 has no resin. It also says H-DUAL is falsified if 'this acrylic-only composition' reaches low drift, but S1C02 is not acrylic-only; it contains 0.0% acrylic. The protocol can numerically observe drift below 4.75% or at/above 9.51%, and the 4.76-point gap exceeds the 2-point resolution, but those outcomes can only challenge the transferred E2-core baseline, not falsify H-RESIN or H-DUAL.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A drift difference could be overstated as proof of a specific molecular or encounter-frequency mechanism.
objections.objection: No target-formulation identity, target hold result, or outcome-derived label is visibly used, so no outcome leakage is established. The scope limitation is that M-HOLD-120 can establish only formulation-level drift behavior; it cannot establish H-RESIN's explanatory language that suppression occurs by lowering effective concentration and encounter frequency of reaction-capable species. The proposer generally respects this boundary, but any mechanistic attribution beyond superlinear suppression would exceed the rheological protocol.

skeptic.recommended_change: Either relabel S1C02::M-HOLD-120 strictly as an E2 baseline-transfer experiment and remove all claims of accepting or falsifying H-RESIN and H-DUAL, or expand the experiment into a process-matched E2-centered modifier design. At minimum, run unmodified E2, an acrylic-only formulation, and an acrylic-plus-minor-tackifier formulation; preferably include tackifier-only as a 2-by-2 axis design. Freeze each reactive mass fraction and its E1_drift times phi_r prediction before measurement, use at least two independently prepared replicates per cell, randomize run order, and enforce the same recorded preparation and melt history. This would test superlinear suppression and allow the acrylic-only versus tackifier-containing comparison required by H-DUAL.
skeptic.strongest_objection: S1C02 activates neither modifier axis, gives H-CORE, H-RESIN, and H-DUAL the identical 9.51% prediction, and therefore separates zero registered hypothesis pairs; the card-level claims that it can accept or falsify H-RESIN or H-DUAL are invalid.

tool_trace.name: get_state_aware_rheology_summary
tool_trace.reason: This upstream material-structure evidence must be loaded first to determine how realization state, shared thermal response, and hold drift should govern subsequent experiment comparison.

claim_boundaries: The shared-shape/state-shift structure is established only within the measured local chemistry family.
The apparent E_eta descriptor is rheological, not a chemical reaction activation energy.
The E1/E5 hold contrast does not identify a unique molecular mechanism.
The phosphoric-acid-labelled E1 +P curve is not used in the chemistry-audited primary state model.
No validation-formulation identity or outcome is used by this tool.
design_rules: Represent a candidate as formulation plus process/realization state, not composition alone.

Use one state-specific anchor measurement to locate a new realization or nearby local formulation on the transferable thermal-response shape when it remains inside the supported local chemistry family.
Treat static viscosity, temperature response and thermal-hold stability as separate decision variables.
When the failure mode is hot-hold drift, choose an experiment and measurement window that directly test drift rather than only matching one nominal viscosity value.
Use external resin/tackifier evidence to define chemically plausible directions, but do not convert analogue proximity into a predicted local outcome.

one_point_state_calibration.interpretation: Within the tested local chemistry family, one state-specific viscosity anchor can locate a previously held-out nominal formulation on the shared thermal-response shape to roughly 6-10% pooled multiplicative error.
one_point_state_calibration.validation_scheme: leave one nominal formulation out; fit shared shape on the remaining formulations; use one anchor from the held formulation

state_shift_master_curve.interpretation: Within the chemistry-audited local family, a realization-specific viscosity-scale intercept plus a shared quadratic inverse-temperature response closes the data far better than a formulation-level intercept using the same thermal basis.

temporal_stability_coordinate.interpretation: Original E1 and E5 hold trajectories show that thermal-hold viscosity drift is strongly formulation dependent and should be treated separately from static viscosity.

thermal_coordinate.interpretation: The apparent temperature-sensitivity descriptor remains comparatively concentrated after chemistry auditing; it is a rheological descriptor, not a molecular reaction activation energy.

experiment_design_implications.hold_window: For the current local study, 120 C and the common 15-60 min window directly interrogate the observed instability while matching the available validation window.
experiment_design_implications.selection_target: Select a formulation-process point that is informative about the observed instability and state uncertainty, not merely the closest static-viscosity value.
experiment_design_implications.state_anchor: A single in-range anchor can be used for efficient local curve calibration; 120 C is operationally attractive because it is also the hold-stability test temperature.

provenance_audit.reason: The source record is phosphoric-acid-labelled and its additive identity/amount is not represented in formulations.csv; it is retained as sensitivity-only until chemistry is reconciled.

result.source_scope: original pre-validation local measurements with chemistry-comparability audit

tool_trace.name: get_candidate_hypothesis
tool_trace.reason: The admissible E2-anchored candidate axes, historical boundary, and independent acrylic-like and tackifier-like variations are needed before candidate experiment cards can be judged.

evidence: PAT_US20160215185A1: repeated acrylic tackifying resin examples at approximately 19-20% of total formulation
PAT_US6465104B1 Example 10: 25 wt% low-OH acrylic copolymer with direct 121 C viscosity-stability data
PAPER_CN_ADHESIVES_2025_34_09_54: reports a 15% preferred acrylic-resin addition level, retained as directional lower-bound evidence until its fraction denominator is reverified
acrylic_like_modifier_pct_total.interpretation: 20 and 25% are directly commensurate coarse anchors in the current curated record. The 15% grid level is retained as a lower-bound design point, but the literature denominator for the reported 15% addition level is not treated as an exact total-formulation anchor until reverified.

evidence: PAT_US5932680A: examples around 4.8-6.4% tackifying/hydrocarbon resin and preferred resin range 3-10 wt%
PAT_US20070155859A1: tackifiers/rheology-control agents typically used below about 10 wt%
minor_tackifier_like_modifier_pct_total.interpretation: 5% represents the repeatedly documented minor-resin region and 10% is a conservative coarse upper level.

result.claim_boundary: External examples are analogues. They support candidate-family and coarse-region hypotheses, not an exact optimum for AC1920/TK100 and not a proven local molecular mechanism. The current reconstruction uses only pre-result evidence at runtime; the exact validation coordinates and outcome are excluded from candidate construction, ranking and tie-breaking.

decision_policy.claim_boundary: This policy can recover an evidence-supported formulation neighborhood, but it is not a predictor of the exact wet-lab optimum.

acrylic_like.basis: 15% directional lower-region evidence plus directly commensurate ~19-20% examples; 25% remains directly supported but is a larger perturbation.

minor_tackifier_like.basis: Curated PUR examples repeatedly place tackifying/hydrocarbon resin near 5%, with broader guidance below about 10%.

experiment_intents.causal_isolation: Use when the primary objective is attribution of one formulation axis. Prefer a single active modifier axis only in this mode.
experiment_intents.performance_mitigation: Use when a measured failure mode is already established and the next experiment is intended to reduce that failure. Independently supported multi-modifier interventions are admissible.
experiment_intents.uncertainty_resolution: Use when missing process, stoichiometric or evidence information prevents an interpretable performance test.

decision_policy.purpose: Select an experimentally informative intervention from pre-result evidence without treating a literature composition as the hidden optimum.
ranking_rules: Exact distance to an external analogue anchor is audit metadata, not a primary optimization objective.
Candidates in the same evidence-support class are not rewarded merely for being numerically closer to a literature percentage.
For performance mitigation, two modifier axes may be combined when each is independently supported and the combination stays inside bounded evidence regions.

Among candidates with comparable evidence coverage and interpretability, prefer the smallest sufficient total modifier burden and the smallest justified departure from the characterized local chemistry.
A single-variable design is preferred only when causal attribution is the stated experiment intent; it is not a universal default.
Held-out validation coordinates and outcomes must never enter candidate construction, ranking or tie-breaking.

historical_status.interpretation: The prospective historical claim attaches to the Agent recommendation itself. The current coarse grid and fine-refinement software are later reproducible operationalizations of the evidence-constrained region and are not represented as the original contemporaneous freeze algorithm unless older provenance is recovered.

local_reactive_core_anchor.reason: E2 is the geometric centre of the original five-point local design: 50/50 PPG2000/PDP-70 and NCO:OH=1.80, centered between E1/E3 stoichiometric perturbations and E4/E5 composition perturbations.
local_reactive_core_anchor.stoichiometry_note: The E2 NCO:OH=1.80 label applies to the original reactive core. If a modifier contributes reactive OH or another NCO-reactive group, true stoichiometry must be recalculated from verified material specifications.

stability_hypotheses.H1_formulation_family: Partial replacement of the reactive-only formulation by an acrylic-like and/or minor tackifier-like resin can reduce hot-hold viscosity drift under matched process conditions.
stability_hypotheses.H2_functionality: At comparable acrylic loading, lower effective reactive-group density or lower-OH acrylic chemistry is expected to be more favorable for hot-hold viscosity stability than more highly reactive acrylic chemistry.
stability_hypotheses.H3_region: A useful candidate region is expected within the externally supported coarse space spanned by 15-25% acrylic-like modifier and 0-10% minor tackifier-like modifier, while preserving the relative E2 reactive-core proportions.

result.agent_hint: Tackifying-resin-modified PUR is an externally documented formulation family; do not restrict the search to fully reactive polyol/isocyanate mixtures.
result.limitation: Single patent example; does not report thermal-hold drift.
result.pattern: polyester polyol + PPG425 + tackifying resin + MDI

result.agent_hint: Hydrocarbon resin can coexist with reactive PUR while retaining measurable melt-processability; include a minor tackifier/hydrocarbon-resin axis rather than fixing the modifier at zero.
result.limitation: Different polyols and application; no thermal-hold stability trajectory.
result.pattern: multiple polyester polyols + PPG425 + hydrocarbon resin + MDI

result.agent_hint: Acrylic-tackifying-resin-modified PUR around 20% of the total formulation is externally documented; 20% is therefore a defensible coarse candidate level, not a value inferred from the local follow-up result.
result.limitation: Different molecular weights, catalysts and application; viscosity is a single-temperature observation, not a hold-stability measurement.
result.pattern: polyoxypropylene diol + polyester diols + acrylic tackifying resin + MDI

result.agent_hint: Repeated examples independently anchor an acrylic-resin design level near 20% while preserving melt processability.
result.limitation: Different chemistry and process history; no causal stability proof.
result.pattern: polyoxypropylene diol + polyester diols + acrylic tackifying resin + MDI

result.agent_hint: The external database supports an acrylic-modified formulation family and provides a reproducible anchor around 20% for coarse candidate generation.
result.limitation: External analogue only; not evidence for the current formulation's exact optimum.
result.pattern: polyoxypropylene diol + polyester diols + acrylic tackifying resin + MDI

result.agent_hint: Multiple neighboring examples reduce the chance that the ~20% acrylic-resin level is a one-off literature artifact.
result.limitation: No thermal-hold curve and no direct match to AC1920/TK100.
result.pattern: polyoxypropylene diol + polyester diols + acrylic tackifying resin + MDI

result.agent_hint: Large viscosity changes across polyol-composition variants show that composition-level changes can strongly alter melt rheology; formulation-family changes are therefore reasonable when the observed failure is large.
result.limitation: Not a resin-modifier study and not a hold-stability experiment.

result.agent_hint: A peer-reviewed PUR study reported 15% acrylic resin as the overall preferred addition level in its system; this independently supports 15% as a coarse acrylic-axis candidate level.
result.limitation: Optimization target was overall high-temperature adhesive performance, not thermal-hold viscosity; chemistry differs from the local system.
result.pattern: polyether polyol + polyphenylene-ether polyol + acrylic resin + crystalline polyester polyol + MDI

result.agent_hint: A 25 wt% low-OH acrylic copolymer formulation showed substantially slower viscosity rise than the equal-loading higher-OH acrylic comparator; this supports both a 25% acrylic candidate level and the hypothesis that lower reactive-group density can improve hot-hold stability.
result.limitation: Different acrylic chemistry and much longer hold window; does not establish the local mechanism.
result.pattern: PPG1000 + PPG2000 + polyester polyol + low-OH acrylic copolymer + MDI

result.agent_hint: At the same 25 wt% acrylic loading, the higher-OH acrylic analogue exhibited roughly twice the reported 8 h viscosity increase of the low-OH example, making modifier functionality a plausible stability variable rather than loading alone.
result.limitation: Patent comparison; acrylic materials are not AC1920 and the result is not a direct local-system measurement.
result.pattern: same formulation as Example 10 but higher-OH acrylic copolymer

result.agent_hint: A functional-tackifier-containing formulation had lower reported stability rise than the no-acrylic/no-functional-tackifier comparator in the same example set, supporting the idea that modifier identity can change hot-melt stability.
result.limitation: Other formulation variables including MDI differ; not an isolated causal comparison.
result.pattern: PPG2025 + PPG4025 + polyester polyol + functional tackifier + MDI

result.agent_hint: The no-acrylic/no-functional-tackifier comparator reported a larger stability value than several modifier-containing examples, providing directional support for a modifier-family hypothesis rather than proof of one optimum.
result.limitation: MDI and other variables differ across the table; use only as directional evidence.
result.pattern: PPG2025 + PPG4025 + polyester polyol + MDI; no acrylic polymer or functional tackifier

result.agent_hint: The patent states that tackifiers and rheology-control agents may be used in small amounts, typically below about 10 wt%, supporting 10% as a conservative upper coarse level for the minor-tackifier axis.
result.limitation: No specific thermal-hold comparison and no exact match to TK100.
result.pattern: polyurethane hot melt with optional tackifiers/plasticizers/rheology-control agents

result.agent_hint: Published formulation art explicitly treats viscosity rise during prolonged hot holding as a design failure mode and cites a preferred stability level of no more than about 25% increase over 4-10 h; this supports thermal-hold stability as an independent design objective.
result.limitation: The time scale is much longer than the local 15-60 min test and should not be converted into a local numerical threshold.
result.pattern: thermally stable reactive hot melt urethane composition

top_cards_in_policy_order.acceptance_criterion: Matched 15-60 min drift at 120 C stays below 4.75% across at least two repeats, i.e. below half the linear-dilution prediction of 9.51% implied by a reactive mass fraction of 1.0000. This accepts H-RESIN over H-CORE.
top_cards_in_policy_order.falsification_criterion: H-RESIN is falsified if matched 15-60 min drift is at or above the linear-dilution prediction of 9.51%. H-CORE is falsified if drift falls below 4.75%, a separation larger than the 2.00% resolution threshold. H-DUAL is falsified if this acrylic-only composition reaches the low-drift regime with no minor tackifier present.

measurement_plan.name: matched-window 120 C thermal hold
measurement_plan.protocol: Hold the melt at 120 C. Record viscosity at 15, 30, 45 and 60 min. Report the 15-60 min matched-window relative change. Run at least two independent repeats.
